item.title: South Africa head coach Erasmus banned for six matches
item.description: Erasmus made the comments at a news conference in Dublin on Monday [Getty Images] South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six matches by World Rugby over comments he made about match officials in his side's Nations Championship defeat by France last week. Speaking at a news conference conference in Dublin on Monday before the Springboks' match with Ireland, Erasmus questioned what he perceived as double standards in officiating to the point where he asked: "is that not match-fixing?". The two-time Rugby World Cup-winning coach was referencing the implementation of new rules surrounding hip-drop and knee-drop tackles, and felt the laws were not being applied correctly. It comes after Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast became the first player to be cited for a hip-drop tackle in Ireland's win over Fiji on Saturday , which was not penalised in-play by referee Angus Gardner and television match official [TMO] Mike Adamson. World Rugby said an independent panel determined that Erasmus' comments "suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match". In response, South Africa Rugby said it has requested a full misconduct hearing and an opportunity for Erasmus to "contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives". It is the third time Erasmus has been sanctioned by World Rugby over his comments about match officials. When he was South Africa's director of rugby, he was suspended for two months by World Rugby after he posted an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' opening Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions in 2021. World Rugby found the video contained "multiple abusive and insulting comments and attacks on the officials". In 2022, he received a two-match ban for a series of tweets criticising officials in a defeat by France. Erasmus' latest ban has been imposed under World Rugby's match official abuse sanction process, which was introduced by the governing body in July. If the suspension is upheld, Erasmus will miss Saturday's game with Ireland in Dublin (16:40 GMT), next week's finals weekend fixture at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium and the start of his side's Rugby Championship campaign next summer. item.description: Peter Storey has died aged 81 -Credit:PA Former England and Arsenal legend Peter Storey has passed away at the age of 81. Storey was an instrumental figure in the Gunners' historic 1971 double-winning squad, playing a pivotal role in securing both the First Division championship and the FA Cup under manager Bertie Mee. Arsenal confirmed the news of his passing on Tuesday, stating via The Mirror : "Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time." Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal over 15 years and remains eighth on the club's all-time list. The North London club intends to honor the club icon ahead of their UEFA Champions League fixture against Borussia Dortmund. His international debut came in 1971 in a commanding 3-0 victory over Greece at Wembley. Storey's journey in soccer began when he joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961, with four years passing before he made his first-team debut, shortly after turning 20. The Surrey-born defender was initially deployed as a left-back in a defeat to Leicester City, yet impressed sufficiently to feature in the remaining 29 matches of that season. Storey cemented his reputation as a 'tough guy' after injuring Manchester City icon Mike Summerbee during the 1966/67 campaign. However, with the arrival of legendary Arsenal manager Mee, Storey firmly established himself as an Arsenal icon, transitioning to right back and midfield as the Gunners transformed into a formidable force. His distinguished career also yielded the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup alongside Arsenal's historic double. Storey's tenure at Arsenal concluded on a bitter note when he was suspended for refusing to train with the reserves, ultimately departing to Fulham on a free transfer in 1977. He played a crucial role in helping the Cottagers stave off relegation in a side that boasted the talents of George Best, Bobby Moore and Rodney Marsh, before hanging up his cleats midway through the following season. item.title: 'He discredited the man himself': Ashwin tears into Pat Cummins over Usman Khawaja, makes big Sandpaper-gate claim
item.description: Former India spinner R Ashwin has expressed surprise at the manner in which Australia captain Pat Cummins responded to Usman Khawaja's claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, suggesting that the controversy continues to divide the Australian dressing room even eight years later. In his autobiography, 'Sabr: Finding My Way in Cricket and Life', Khawaja alleged that the entire Australian team knew about the ball-tampering plan. This contradicted the findings of Cricket Australia's investigation, which held only three players, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, responsible. Cummins strongly rejected the claims, describing them as "100% wrong" and "complete and utter nonsense". He also denied knowing that sandpaper had been brought onto the field. Ashwin, however, was taken aback by the Australian captain's response, arguing that he had questioned Khawaja's credibility rather than simply challenging his account. "Firstly, when Usman Khawaja has mentioned certain things in his book, those are his accounts of the story and we need to respect that. But what happened at Pat Cummins's press conference is that he didn't discredit Usman Khawaja's account of the story; he discredited the man himself. And that is the problem for me," Ashwin said on JioStar. "When you can't discredit someone's information, you discredit the person. I know Usman Khawaja; I've played a lot of cricket with him, not on a personal front. He is a man of high integrity and really honest and up-and-straightforward person." The former India off-spinner also pointed out that Cummins, who was on his third tour at the time of the 2018 scandal, was unlikely to have been part of the leadership group. Ashwin believed that group comprised Smith, Warner and possibly Tim Paine. "I genuinely thought that this conversation would have centred around saying, 'I wasn't aware of what exactly was happening. I wasn't a part of the leadership group.' It was very surprising for me that Pat Cummins had to come to the press conference and discredit the person himself. That was a little bit of a shock to me, watching from afar," he added. The scandal erupted during the third Test against South Africa at Newlands in March 2018, when Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball. Smith, Warner and Bancroft were subsequently banned by Cricket Australia. While Ashwin praised Cummins for helping lead Australian cricket's transition alongside Tim Paine after the controversy, he felt recent comments from the captain and Warner indicated that differences over the episode remained. "Pat Cummins, who I really admire as a cricketer, is the captain of Australia and, alongside Tim Paine, took on the new regime of trying to rebrand Australian cricket after that incident. He has come out and called what Khawaja has said baseless, nonsense, and something that does not have proof," Ashwin said. item.title: 'A leader, a finisher, calm and composed under pressure': Cricket fraternity celebrates MS Dhoni's CSK legacy
item.description: NEW DELHI: The end of an era in the IPL! After years of leading Chennai Super Kings to glory, MS Dhoni is officially stepping away from his playing career and taking up the role of mentor at CSK. The announcement has triggered an emotional response from the cricket fraternity, with former teammates and fellow cricketers paying tribute to the man who transformed Chennai into a cricketing powerhouse. Irfan Pathan praised Dhoni's leadership, composure and lasting influence on Indian cricket. "A leader, a finisher, calm and composed under pressure, and one of the most influential figures in Indian cricket. MS Dhoni, the legacy you have created will be hard to match. Well done, MS! I’m sure your immense experience and knowledge will continue to inspire the next generation of cricketers," Pathan wrote on X. Shikhar Dhawan also shared an emotional message, highlighting how Dhoni's influence will extend beyond his playing days: "What an incredible journey it’s been, @msdhoni bhai! Your leadership, calmness and impact on the game have inspired generations. The player may take a step back, but your influence on cricket will continue. Wishing you the very best in this new role with CSK!" wrote Dhawan. CSK's Ruturaj Gaikwad reflected on the lessons he learned from Dhoni, particularly his simplicity and leadership: "Simplicity. I got to learn the exact meaning of this word when I first joined CSK in 2019 by watching you through the lens as much as possible, that was the biggest lesson I learned despite of all the achievements that you have accumulated over the years! To share the dressing room ,the field,the 22 yards and to finish games with you is what are dreams are made of. You are and You Will always Be OUR THAALAA, our captain and our Leader! Thank you Mahi bhai for everything," Ruturaj penned on Instagram. Dhoni's retirement decision reportedly came during a video call with CSK officials while they were discussing player retention. According to co-owner Rupa Gurunath, Dhoni quietly suggested adding his name to the list of players being released. CSK owner N Srinivasan summed up the relationship between the franchise and its legendary captain. "There is no CSK without MS Dhoni. For nearly two decades, we have walked and grown alongside each other, through triumphs, setbacks and everything in between," CSK owner N Srinivasan said in the franchise statement. The numbers tell their own story: five IPL titles, two Champions League T20 trophies, 5,314 IPL runs for CSK and 272 appearances for the franchise. The iconic No. 7 may no longer be seen leading CSK on the field, but his connection with the franchise is far from over. The captain may have stepped aside, but Thala's legacy continues.

item.title: Liam Lawson has been a "revelation" as he earned 2027 Racing Bulls F1 deal - Alan Permane
item.description: Motorsport photo Racing Bulls Formula 1 chief Alan Permane says Liam Lawson's improved 2026 form has been a "revelation", and addressed suggestions of a difference in vision within Red Bull. In a wide-ranging interview with Motorsport.com , Permane addressed why the decision between incumbent Lawson and Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov to partner Arvid Lindblad had taken so long, and why backing Lawson doesn't have to go against the team's manta to bring up young talent. "Having Liam is great for our team, there's no doubt. He's been immense," Permane said. "He's beaten Alpine on his own, if you like. But it's not just about that. It is about developing young talent. And honestly, that is incredibly difficult to do without having a benchmark. "I know there was talk about putting Tsolov in the car, but one of the reasons we have kept Liam is firstly because of how he's performed, no doubt, but it's also about developing for the future. We rate Arvid very, very highly, and this will enable him to develop and it will enable us to see how that's going. Alan Permane, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Alan Permane, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls "Liam has undoubtedly massively improved and Arvid has got all that to look at. We share all that data across cars and what's he doing and how is he getting the most out of the car in the race. And I think that's absolutely invaluable for Arvid." There are strong suggestions the delayed decision was prompted by a difference in vision between the various stakeholders involved in the decision, which not only includes Permane but also the wider Red Bull company, including Permane's boss Oliver Mintzlaff as well as Red Bull Racing boss Laurent Mekies. But Permane echoed Mekies in insisting the call was made by Racing Bulls. " Laurent has been very clear in the press that the decision is not his," Permane insisted. "It's a Racing Bulls decision and I'm responsible for sporting [matters] at Racing Bulls. That's clear. However, I have a boss, Oliver Mintzlaff, and we have shareholders as well. "A decision as important as this isn't just made by myself. It's made by myself in conjunction with my boss and the shareholders, making sure they're happy. And the reason it's taken a little bit longer than you guys would like, honestly, is that I was just taking my time and making sure we got to the right decision." item.title: Nease's unlikely game-winner adds to Panther football lore
item.description: Northeast Florida's playoff moment of the year so far came from a No. 24 lined up as an offensive lineman, one with no recorded touches on the football all season. With zero rushing yards and zero receiving yards in 2026, Nease junior Ethan Fennelly was an unlikely choice for postseason's brightest highlight. But the Panthers' fullback made his first stat of the season one to remember when he caught Aiden Phifer 's two-point conversion pass with 35 seconds left to defeat Pace 35-34 in the Florida High School Athletic Association Region 1-5A football quarterfinal on Nov. 13. After Chase Phifer had caught Aiden Phifer's 25-yard touchdown to cut the lead to one, Nease coach Collin Drafts took the gamble and went for two, and Fennelly — lined up as an eligible tackle, going to the ground on a cut block and getting back up to catch Aiden Phifer's toss wide-open in the end zone — became the hero of the evening. It's a play likely to earn a lasting place in Nease postseason lore, which already includes Tim Tebow 's heroics in the mid-2000s and the 244-yard receiving effort by Dom Henry and the winning kick by Canaan Kimball to oust Spruce Creek in the 2021 regionals. Nease football now carries a seven-game winning run into Friday's battle against Gainesville Buchholz at Citizens Field, with one of North Florida's premier offensive weapons still red-hot: Senior wide receiver Tyshawn Ford surpassed 1,500 all-purpose yards for the season in the win over Pace. Wolfpack soccer on fire early It might be the Gateway Conference's most frustrating drought: Duval County public schools are nearing 50 seasons without an FHSAA state champion in boys soccer, despite years of near-misses for Fletcher, Mandarin, Stanton and White. This year, watch out for Wolfson. Despite early-season injury woes, the Wolfpack are off to a 5-0 start, downing previously-unbeaten Fleming Island 4-2 on home turf in a rain-slickened Nov. 16 game. Kai Gehring scored twice, Ricardo Mejia found the net only 77 seconds in and speedy winger William Reid tacked on another one. MaxPreps hasn't yet issued its first set of rankings for 2026-27, but when the numbers come out, Wolfson appears in line for a high position in Class 3A. Wolfson, with third-year keeper Leonardo Bustamante in the net, next takes on Episcopal on Nov. 18 and Stanton on Nov. 20 ahead of what could be a gigantic showdown against 2025-26 state runner-up Mandarin on Nov. 23. item.title: Swansea boss Matos on brink of Strasbourg move
item.description: Swansea boss Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Vitor Matos is on the brink of leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg. Matos, 38, is understood to have said goodbye to players and staff at the Swans' Fairwood training base on Tuesday after Strasbourg made an official approach for the Swansea head coach. There is no confirmation yet that a deal has been agreed between the clubs, but Strasbourg are thought to be ready to pay in the region of £5m to secure the Portuguese's services. News of Strasbourg's interest had emerged on Monday, with Matos - who is under contract at Swansea until 2030 - telling the Championship club he wanted to leave. Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to depart. That will leave Swansea stalwarts Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary as the only remaining senior staff members at the club. Matos had been due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month. Current Strasbourg boss Hugo Oliveira, Matos' fellow countryman, has been under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches. Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to take over at Ipswich Town – in July. O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone. Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea. Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November. The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign. Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot going into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion. Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea. item.title: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares detained by ICE in Texas: 'This is crazy'
item.description: Venezuela's boxer Jorge Linares, left, exchanges punches with Panama's Whyber Garcia during a World Boxing Association championship for the super featherweight title in Panama City. (AP) Former three-division world boxing champion Jorge Luis Linares Palencia, 41, has been detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in El Paso, Texas. The Venezuelan athlete's detention prompted questions about why he was taken into federal custody, despite his attorneys' claims that he is legally in the country. Linares first disclosed his detention Sunday in a brief post on X: "ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy," he wrote in Spanish . The retired boxer is being held at the El Paso Processing Center, according to federal detention records reviewed by the Express-News. As of Tuesday, the circumstances surrounding his detention remain unclear, and immigration officials have not publicly disclosed what prompted the action. On Monday, immigration law firm Wilner & O'Reilly confirmed it was representing Linares and disputed any suggestion that he was unlawfully present in the United States. "Mr. Linares is legally present in the United States and has cooperated fully with the authorities," the firm said in a statement to Agence France-Presse. "We are working closely with ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to resolve this matter as quickly as possible," the attorneys added. "Immigration attorneys are handling his case, and I am in constant contact with his family," Mendoza wrote on X. "As WBA President, I will always support our champions, in and out of the ring. Stay strong, Jorge." Nicknamed "The Golden Boy," Linares captured world championships across three weight divisions - featherweight, super featherweight and lightweight - during a professional career spanning more than two decades. He retired in October 2023 following a loss to British boxer Jack Catterall, finishing with 47 victories, including 29 knockouts, and nine defeats. item.title: Trieu: Michigan gets commitment from Ohio offensive lineman
item.description: Michigan added to its 2027 recruiting class on Tuesday, Nov. 17, with the addition of Chillicothe (Ohio) offensive tackle Conner Rutherford. The 6-foot-6, 300-pound Rutherford was committed to NC State, but recently re-opened his recruitment after the firing of head coach Dave Doeren. The Wolverines then came in with an offer and got him on campus for a visit for the Michigan State game. Rutherford has 29 scholarship offers in total, but cited the academics, chance to compete at the Big Ten level, and Michigan’s staff as reasons he was making this choice. In him, the Wolverines get a big, strong, physical player who is still learning the game after picking up football later than most. “He’s only been playing football since eighth grade,” said Darren Gammell of DJRS, a recruiting organization in Ohio that has been working with Rutherford since his sophomore year. “He is a smart, intelligent kid who had his focus on school. He skipped a whole grade, he was so smart. So he played baseball, but nothing super serious. Now he loves football and wishes he had started earlier.” Rutherford just turned 17 years old, and could be in the 2028 class had he stayed with his class through grade school. But he went from not knowing how to play to becoming a national recruit in a short period of time. “To be honest with you, he has gotten way more versatile,” Gammell said. “He's able to actually run all four positions, rather than just tackle. He’s improved a lot on his feet and striking. He just needed to improve more on the technicalities of being a lineman.” Michigan is recruiting Ohio heavily in the 2027 and 2028 classes. That includes prioritizing Rutherford’s junior teammate, prolific four-star running back Cartae Ligon. The Wolverines’ staff has been working to show that recruiting the surrounding areas, which includes the talent in Ohio is important, and Rutherford has bought in to their vision. “Ultimately, you have to look at the past. Now isn’t going to show what this staff is about,” Gammell said, “We know the circumstances. They just got there this past winter. They haven’t even been there a year. Coach Harding has some elite development. He had two first-rounders at Utah, pretty darn impressive. Coach Harding being an Ohio guy himself, that’s also something that moved the needle, and allowed them to build a relationship fairly fast. On top of that, Coach Whittingham’s success over his career as a head coach is legit. So you have the history of Michigan and the offensive line development of the staff.” Michigan now has 23 commits in their 2027 class. Rutherford now makes five offensive linemen in that group. item.description: Brandon Cisse’s early exit with an injury added to the Green Bay Packers’ troubles during Sunday’s divisional matchup. The Packers struggled to make an impact on either side of the ball, allowing the Minnesota Vikings to leave Lambeau Field with a convincing 30-10 victory. The Packers rookie injured his ribs in the opening quarter while trying to bring down Vikings wide receiver Myles Price following Kirk Cousins’ 38-yard touchdown pass. However, USA Today’s Ryan Wood shared encouraging news on X (formerly Twitter), reporting that head coach Matt LaFleur had provided a positive update on the rookie’s condition. Price managed to stay upright through contact from the rookie cornerback and complete the 38-yard touchdown in the end zone. The collision left the Green Bay defender on the turf, where he received medical attention before being taken to the locker room. item.title: Jeremy Fowler signs new multiyear deal with ESPN
item.description: Bristol, CT - April 24, 2018 - Studio W: Jeremy Fowler during a SportsCenter Special: NFL Nation Mock Draft. (Photo by Melissa Rawlins / ESPN Images) Few people have gained more from ESPN’s acquisition of NFL Network than Jeremy Fowler. According to Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal , Fowler has signed a new multi-year contract to remain at ESPN as an NFL insider and senior national writer. The agreement also widens his footprint across both ESPN and NFL Network. Fowler will appear more regularly on NFL Live , Good Morning Football, SportsCenter , and The Aftermath — hosted by Zubin Mehenti and Herm Edwards — which NFL Network launched as its flagship Monday afternoon program in September. Fowler joined ESPN in 2014 after serving as a national college football insider for CBSSports.com. Since then, he has become one of the network’s most dependable newsbreakers after Adam Schefter, moving between reported features for ESPN’s digital platforms and weekend SportsCenter appearances. His television work had already started spilling onto NFL Network before this deal, too, as OutKick reported in August that Fowler and Dan Graziano were expected to contribute to The Insiders alongside Schefter. Fowler’s new contract is the latest in a string of deals ESPN has struck with its NFL news operation since taking control of NFL Network this spring. Ian Rapoport, Schefter’s longtime rival for scoops, reportedly agreed to a four-year deal in April and formally signed in June . Schefter followed with an extension after reports that ESPN was closing in on a deal that would keep him at the network several years into the 2030s. Fowler’s growing workload across both networks suggests ESPN sees him as an important part of its effort to blend its own NFL coverage with NFL Network’s programming. With Schefter, Rapoport, Graziano, and Fowler now under one corporate roof, it’s still unclear how ESPN will divide airtime among its crowded group of insiders across both channels over the length of Fowler’s new contract. item.title: Rick Hendrick Scrapped His Reprimand, and Larson’s Third Title Followed
item.description: Kyle Larson's No. 5 Chevrolet at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, March 2026. Photo: Nascar9919 via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 Kyle Larson wrapped up his third Cup championship on Lap 78 at Homestead-Miami, when Chase Briscoe’s engine blew and ended the first stage. He then spent the rest of Sunday night bouncing off the wall and finishing 12th. The more revealing moment came months earlier, in a team meeting where Rick Hendrick threw away the speech he had planned to give. That is the story worth chasing, because it says more about how Hendrick Motorsports won this title than the trophy does. The argument here is simple: the most important call of the No. 5 team’s season was a restraint call, and the organization’s own account of it deserves more attention than the final-lap scramble that Ryan Blaney won. The title was decided in stage one Here is the arithmetic NASCAR’s own recap lays out. Larson was running fourth when Briscoe’s pole-winning car expired. Stage points of seven put him beyond the reach of Christopher Bell, who collected eight, and Denny Hamlin, who took five. Joe Gibbs Racing’s pair were the only other drivers still alive mathematically, and they were left to fight over second. Crew chief Cliff Daniels collected his third title, all with Larson. Rick Hendrick’s radio message to his driver: “Now you can run the wall.” Larson did exactly that, then finished 12th while Blaney passed Tyler Reddick on Lap 266 of 267 to win. William Byron, who had been leading by just over a second before the final caution, took third for Hendrick. Larson became the first back-to-back champion since Jimmie Johnson’s run of five straight, and Blaney’s win moved him to fourth in the final standings, 94 points back. Denny Hamlin (No. 11) and Kyle Larson (No. 5) side by side at Dover in 2024. Photo: Zach Catanzareti Photo / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0. The speech that never happened Hendrick’s own telling, given in the Homestead media room, goes like this. Over the summer, the organization’s four teams were struggling to find speed in a new Chevrolet body, with mixed results. Hendrick said he walked toward a team meeting ready to ask what was wrong with everyone. At the last second he told Jeff Gordon the room needed pressure taken off instead, and he told the group that the answer might take weeks or the rest of the year. Gordon, who is vice chairman, said the team expected and deserved a dressing-down and got the reverse. He credited Hendrick with reading the room correctly. Hendrick said that meeting opened a floodgate of shared information, and called it the best of the year. Treat that as what it is: a winning organization narrating its own turning point, with the benefit of hindsight. It is still a primary account from the people in the room. item.description: The ATP hierarchy has come under fire following a controversial decision at the ATP Finals. Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara walked onto the Turin court on Monday and collected their trophies for ending the 2026 season as the doubles world number ones. The singles players took part in a glamorous, suited-and-booted photoshoot, while the doubles players wore their tennis kits, and were photographed in the stands. item.title: Max Anderson Lands on the Tigers’ Trade Candidate List
item.description: Max Anderson has hit at every level the Detroit Tigers have sent him to, and he still does not have a spot on the 40-man roster. That squeeze is the reason MLB.com named the second baseman Detroit’s trade candidate going into the 2026-27 offseason. Mark Feinsand of MLB.com published a rundown of one trade candidate for every club on Monday, and Anderson is the name next to the Tigers . Feinsand wrote: “A second-round pick in the 2023 Draft, Anderson has put together a pair of impressive seasons at Double-A and Triple-A, but the 24-year-old still isn’t on the 40-man roster and isn’t a lock to be part of the 2027 club. With Hao-Yu Lee capable of handling second-base duties, Anderson — who won a Minor League Gold Glove Award in 2026 — could be expendable in the right deal given the glut of infield talent in the organization.” Mar 6, 2026; Lakeland, Florida, USA; Detroit Tigers second baseman Max Anderson (82) throws to first during the first inning against the Boston Red Sox at Publix Field at Joker Marchant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mike Watters-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Max Anderson hit his way through Triple-A in 2026 Anderson played 113 minor league games in 2026, 108 of them with Triple-A Toledo and five at Single-A Lakeland. He hit .302 with 17 home runs and 61 RBIs, along with six stolen bases on eight attempts. His on-base percentage was .386, his slugging percentage was .486, and his OPS was .872 . His Mud Hens line on its own was .302/.386/.477 with 24 doubles. The bat is not the only part of the case. Anderson won a Minor League Gold Glove Award at second base in 2026, and he was named one of the Tigers’ prospects of the year by MLB Pipeline in October. Two years of production and an award for the defense still have not bought him a roster spot. Detroit’s 40-man infield is already full The infielders on the Tigers 40-man roster are Javier Baez, Tsung-Che Cheng, Jace Jung, Colt Keith, Hao-Yu Lee, Kevin McGonigle, John Peck, Trey Sweeney and Spencer Torkelson. If Detroit is going to make room for a player like Anderson, it may have to trade a player like Baez, who is entering the final year of his six-year, $140 million contract at $24 million in 2027. Sweeney is another name the Tigers should consider moving off of to open a spot. Second base is the tightest square on that board, and it is already the subject of its own argument in Detroit . Feinsand’s reasoning runs through Lee, who the Tigers believe can handle the position every day. That is what turns a Gold Glove winner hitting .302 at Triple-A into a trade chip instead of a starter. What Detroit should want in return The only way the Tigers should trade Anderson is if they get a proven player back, or a young one with real upside like Baltimore Orioles second baseman Jackson Holliday. Short of that, Detroit needs to find him a 40-man spot some way, somehow.

item.title: Former Celtic star makes surprising Martin O’Neill admission in Brendan Rodgers comparison
item.description: Former Celtic star makes surprising Martin O’Neill admission in Brendan Rodgers comparison Former Celtic defender Charlie Mulgrew has highlighted the significant tactical differences between Martin O’Neill’s original Celtic side and the teams managed by Brendan Rodgers and Ange Postecoglou. With O’Neill now back in charge at Celtic, questions have been raised about how much football has evolved since his hugely successful first spell in Glasgow. Speaking on The Breakdown, Mulgrew suggested that modern players require considerably more tactical guidance than those from his own generation, having spent much of his Celtic career playing under Neil Lennon. “Put it this way, right? If Martin O’Neill had me, Scott Brown, Joe Ledley, Mark Wilson, to name a few. If he had us in that dressing room when we played, we would have that whole building behind the manager. “The reason is because we were brought up in a generation that wasn’t tactics. We took responsibility for what we did. We would just say, ‘we need to win games’, so we would take responsibility. There would never be any tactics. “There’s a generation of players there that have been brought up with tactics. With a clear identity, with unbelievable organisation. When I talk about Brendan Rodgers and Ange Postecoglou, you name those two managers in recent times that have been really successful, where trebles were really normal. “Now those boys are going. That’s what they see as normal. This generation has been brought up with a tactical side. We never got tactics. If it wasn’t going right, Neil Lennon would two-foot the tactics board and go nuts at us. “If anyone turned around and said ‘He was out of order with the way he spoke to us’, Aye, he was, but we should win games! Just win the game. It’s a different generation. This generation of players now demand a certain way and guidance. The level of football has went to another level of information. “For example, I’d love to see an Ange Postecoglou team or a Brendan Rodgers team play against Martin O’Neill’s team. item.title: ‘I didn’t realise’: LeBron James says he picked up ‘bad habits’ while watching Michael Jordan
item.description: Credit: Sarah Stier/Alexander Hassenstein/Bongarts via Getty Images Michael Jordan is arguably the greatest basketball player of all time. The Chicago Bulls icon is a hero to many in the game, so much so that today’s superstars grew up watching and trying to emulate him. LeBron James is one such player, but he has now opened up on the mistake he made while trying to copy Jordan. LeBron James reveals the ‘bad habits’ he picked up while trying to copy Michael Jordan Jordan’s shooting was absolutely unbelievable. The way the NBA legend would step back and find the bucket was just a joy to watch, and every youngster at the time tried to copy that. James was in high school when he started to imitate Jordan, but after studying the game well, he has realised that he was picking up bad habits. Jordan’s fadeaways saw him leaning back while making the shot, which James found really cool and wanted to copy. But what he failed to understand was how imbalanced he got, unlike his idol. He said on the Mind The Game podcast : “My shooting journey is literally watching Michael Jordan. But the thing I didn’t realise is how balanced Michael Jordan was at fadeaways. “I saw a fadeaway. So when I started to see that I had some athletic genes, I maybe picked up some bad habits in my shooting because I could emulate that. “So I was shooting fadeaways as like a freshman in high school. I would make them, but I didn’t realise that I was picking up bad habits along that time because I didn’t study the fact that, okay, MJ’s doing that, but you’re not even seeing how on balance he is. “You have no idea and he’s been doing this for years and years and years and you’re just trying to pick it up because you’re trying to emulate him.” James concluded by saying: “I didn’t know the details as a kid enough about shooting. All I knew was, he was making shots and he was fading and it looked cool. So I’m going to try to do that.” This is a really good insight for any young player dreaming of being an NBA star one day. Trying to emulate your idol’s shooting is great, but if you do it without understanding every aspect of the move, you will pick up some bad habits. Once that’s in, it’s very difficult to get it out – just ask James. He admitted that he still leans back like Jordan did while attempting his fadeaways. It’s the second time the playoff has expanded since it began in 2024, going from the original four teams to 12 teams in 2024 and now to 24 teams beginning next season. The format voted on will secure autobids for each of the ‘power four’ conference champions (ACC, Big 12, Big Ten and SEC) as well as one for the highest-ranked conference champion from the ‘group of six’ (American, Confernce USA, MAC, Mountain West and Pac-12). item.description: Jai Opetaia could be out of his fight with Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard. On 11 December, Fury and Joshua will headline at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium in arguably the biggest British fight ever , and this month brought the news that Opetaia would box Wilder in the chief-support bout . However, boxing insider Dan Rafael tweeted on Tuesday: “Per sources, Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from the Deontay Wilder fight set for Dec. 11 on the #FuryJoshua Netflix undercard. Deontay Wilder (pictured) was due to fight Jai Opetaia (Getty) “The plan is for Wilder to still fight if they can find a suitable replacement and one distinct possibility is a rematch with Derek Chisora.” The unbeaten Opetaia was due to make his heavyweight debut against former world champion Wilder, having recently held the IBF cruiserweight title. Opetaia, 31, was stripped of his cruiserweight belt after signing with the controversial Zuffa Boxing, whose president Dana White has advised Saudi matchmaker Turki Alalshikh on the Fury vs “AJ” undercard, per Joshua’s promoter Eddie Hearn – who said White contractually cannot be involved in the event. Rafael’s reference to a possible rematch between Wilder, 41, and Chisora, 42, comes after the American beat “Delboy” in April, outpointing him in a 12-round brawl in London. However, cruiserweight-turned-heavyweight Richard Riakporhe has already offered to step in for Opetaia. “I hear Jai Opetaia is injured,” the Briton tweeted. “@BronzeBomber I will fight you on less than 4 weeks notice. Wilder secured a controversial draw with Fury in 2018 before suffering stoppage losses to the “Gypsy King” in 2020 and 2021. item.title: Commonwealth medallist Lobban switches from Scotland to Australia
item.description: Greg Lobban has represented Scotland at three Commonwealth Games [Getty Images] Scottish-born squash player Greg Lobban will represent Australia for the first time at this week's China Open. The 34-year-old, who was born in Inverness and has represented Scotland at three Commonwealth Games, confirmed his Australian citizenship had been approved on Tuesday, saying he will now "get to play under the Australian flag". Lobban won a doubles bronze medal for Scotland at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and has 16 PSA titles to his name. The news is therefore a blow to Scottish squash but does not come as a surprise. In an interview with BBC Scotland in June, the world number 29 confirmed he was in the process of applying for citizenship in Australia and believed it was "the best decision for me and my family". Lobban, who has an Australian wife, added that the lure of potentially playing at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles - where the sport will make its Games debut - hastened an already planned move. "I have got strong Australian ties with my wife being born there and my son being half Australian, so this was going to happen at some point," he said. "I was thinking it was probably going to be post-squash career in terms of applying for residency and citizenship, but the prospect of representing Australia at the Olympics is too much of an exciting opportunity to turn down. "At this stage of my career, this is really motivation to put in a good two years and hopefully be able to have Australian representation at the Games." item.description: Michigan added to their 2027 class on Tuesday with the addition of Chillicothe (Ohio) offensive tackle Conner Rutherford . Rutherford (6-6, 300 pounds) was committed to NC State, but re-opened his recruitment after the firing of head coach Dave Doeren. He visited Michigan earlier in the month and now chooses the Wolverines. “They’re the right choice, because I know it’s somewhere I can get a great education, and play against the best players in the country,” Rutherford said. “I feel the staff was very open and welcoming, so it was very easy for us to make that fast connection.” Rutherford did not play football until 8th grade, but picked up the game quickly and became a heavily-recruited player with nearly 30 scholarship offers. He is a physical right tackle prospect who was also strong enough academically to skip a grade, so he just turned 17 and could be in the 2028 class. In addition to football, he has done some wrestling and also played baseball growing up. He is also planning to enroll mid-year and go through spring practice with Michigan. Rutherford is the second recent offensive line addition for Michigan in the 2027 class. They flipped in-state Stanford commit Braden Chaffin earlier this month. Rivals has Rutherford ranked the No. 50 offensive tackle nationally. He is a three-star prospect with an 88 rating.

item.title: IMG Academy adding beach volleyball, tabs Olympic gold medalist as first coach
item.description: For years, some Florida families interested in beach volleyball have looked west for opportunities to develop their game. IMG Academy hopes to change that. The Bradenton-based academy is adding girls' beach volleyball as its 21st sport, creating another avenue for female student-athletes to train and compete without having to leave the state to find elite-level instruction. More: What does an IMG football player's daily life look like? We shadowed one to find out "I hear stories that families from Florida are flying to train in California or sending their kids to stay in Manhattan Beach so they can train in beach," IMG Academy volleyball director Gilad Doron exclusively told USA TODAY Sports. "Well, now they don't have to. You can come here, you can be at school here, and hopefully we'll have some of the same resources and the ability to train them and compete year-round." IMG announced Tuesday, Nov. 17, that Olympic gold medalist Ricardo Santos will lead the new program as its first head coach. The Brazilian competed in four Olympic Games, winning gold in Athens in 2004, silver in Sydney in 2000 and bronze in Beijing in 2008. He was also a two-time world player of the year and was inducted into the International Volleyball Hall of Fame in 2021. “I've spent my career competing and coaching at the highest levels of beach volleyball, and I know what it takes to succeed in this sport,” Santos said in a release. “At IMG Academy, we have an opportunity to build something special for young athletes, combining high-level training with the discipline, confidence and preparation they'll need to succeed in college and beyond.” The program will feature six outdoor courts on IMG's West Campus, with camps scheduled to begin in summer 2027 and the boarding school program following in fall 2027. For Doron, the addition is another opportunity to build something from the ground up. He previously helped establish the beach volleyball program at the University of San Francisco and brings experience in both indoor and beach volleyball to IMG's growing operation. The sport has continued to gain traction at the collegiate level, with NCAA participation increasing 194% over the past decade. More than 11,500 girls participated in high school beach volleyball during the 2024-25 school year, according to the National Federation of State High School Associations. IMG introduced girls' indoor volleyball in 2023 before adding boys' volleyball in 2026 . Beach volleyball represents the latest step in the academy's broader investment in the sport. Doron sees an opportunity to develop more than just another high school program, with hopes of establishing IMG as a destination for younger athletes looking to take their beach volleyball careers to the next level. "If we can do it successfully here, it can be, again, an amazing training center for youth beach to be ready for college or even beyond," Doron said.
